newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate dips 10.653 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate dips 10.653 pct.

text.p: The Philippine benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate slipped to an average of 10.653 percent in Monday's regular weekly auction from last week's 10.693 percent, the Bureau of Treasury said.
The other maturities also fell due to high liquidity in the market, traders said.
The 182-day bill rate fell to an average of 11.067 percent from 11.293 percent; and the 364-day rate tumbled to 11.504 from 11.724 percent.
The auction had tenders totalling 19.010 billion pesos, of which 4.5 billion pesos were awarded.
The amount of tenders showed the high liquidity in the system caused by the imposition of a 20 percent tax on term reverse repos, traders said, This had discouraged banks to reinvest their money.
"The market is so liquid. Banks have to invest their money in alternative instruments," a foreign bank dealer said.
